# Tagcast 1.0 — Your collection, carefully kept

Tagcast brings your iBroadcast collection, metadata editing and listening together
in one independent desktop app. Browse your music, improve album and track details,
review every proposed change and keep listening through the same player and queue.
Your local music files are never changed.

## A smaller player when you want it

The desktop Mini Player keeps artwork, track information, transport and seeking
close together, with optional Always on top. Switching between it and Tagcast's
main window preserves the same playback engine and queue. It also works with the
existing experimental Gapless mode; no second player starts in the background.

## Bring fragmented albums together

Search for an album, **Select all on this page**, then choose **Merge albums…**.
Choose which existing album to keep, review its tracks and confirm. Tagcast checks
the current library before sending once and verifies the result afterwards.

This combines 2–20 complete single-disc entries, up to 500 active tracks. Track
IDs, titles, performers, credits, artwork and track numbers are preserved. The
destination keeps its album metadata and rating; source album ratings and local
album favourites are not transferred. Multi-disc sets and differing disc numbers
are excluded. This does not merge artist identities and has no automatic Undo.

## Find albums by their upload history

Enable **Upload folders** or **Date uploaded** in **Settings → Interface → Sidebar**.
They are off by default. Open a stored folder or day to see familiar album cards,
then search, sort, page or open a complete album.

An album qualifies when at least one of its tracks belongs to that group, so the
same album can appear on several days or in several folders. Opening or playing
it uses the whole album. Stored upload metadata is retained; no local folders are
opened, files scanned or upload feature introduced.

## Safer saves and an updated desktop runtime

Interrupted metadata, cleanup, rating and artwork requests are no longer silently
replayed. Tagcast checks uncertain results against a fresh library instead of
assuming a lost reply means failure. It stops subsequent writes after uncertainty,
preserves partial results and requires fresh conflict checks for another reviewed
action. Safe library reads retain bounded retries and OAuth refresh is preserved.
Remote saves remain non-transactional; read-back cannot make them atomic.

The desktop runtime is updated to **Electron 44.9.3**, including the official
certificate-blocking security mitigation. Automated audio checks now require
complete measurements and a real failing process exit when a required test fails.

## Experimental Gapless remains opt-in

Gapless remains **experimental and disabled by default**, primarily measured with
compatible Original FLAC tracks in normal album order. It requires suitable
iBroadcast streaming access. Shuffle, random albums, playlists and active queue
synchronisation use ordinary playback. Unsupported transitions and failures fall
back to normal playback. There is no crossfade or silence trimming.

Deterministic tests verify their measured PCM inputs; they do not establish
universal sample accuracy for every format, platform, playback speed or output
device. MP3 timing support is separately experimental. See
[Gapless setup and limitations](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v1.0.0/docs/gapless-playback.md).

## Upgrading and service limits

Quit the old app before opening the new version. It uses the normal production
settings/profile locations, retaining preferences, credentials and local favourites.
An isolated Gapless Test profile is not automatically migrated. Keep a backup of
your settings before upgrading; Tagcast does not write local music files.

iBroadcast controls storage, bandwidth, track availability and Premium capabilities.
Its [announced subscription changes](https://news.ibroadcast.com/an-important-update-on-ibroadcast-s-pricing)
can affect which uploads are visible. Tagcast does not promise unlimited storage,
unlock Premium capabilities or provide complete iBroadcast feature parity.

Standalone targets remain macOS Apple Silicon/Intel, Windows x64 and Linux x64.
macOS requires Ventura 13 or newer. Linux requires a graphical session and compatible
system libraries. macOS builds are ad-hoc signed for integrity, not Developer ID
notarized; Windows builds are not Authenticode signed. Source/Python browser use
remains available. All four platform archives pass build and extracted-app checks.
Automated PCM tests use Linux Electron and local macOS synthetic fixtures; real-world
listening acceptance was reported on macOS. These checks do not certify every
physical output device or every Windows/Linux desktop environment.
